_meta.rule: HOTLINES: NEVER add or edit a hotline/text-line number without a human verifying it against an authoritative source (source=national_verified, verified=true). EMERGENCY numbers (police/ambulance/fire): emitted only under the owner's cited-sources standard of 2026-10-29 — >=2 independent agreeing sources, >=1 official, source=multi_source_cited (CIRISAgent#1248). A wrong crisis number is catastrophically worse than the directory fallback.

emergency_india_112.name: Emergency services
emergency_india_112.description: Unified emergency number (police, ambulance, fire; ERSS)
emergency_india_112.validation_notes: CITED 2026-10-29 (CIRISAgent#1248) under the owner's cited-sources standard (>=2 independent agreeing sources, >=1 official; no human check). Sources: UK FCDO travel advice: UK FCDO travel advice, Getting help: "Emergency services in India Telephone: 112 (ambulance, fire, police) These services provide support in English, Hindi and additional languages" (fetched 2026-10-29 via gov.uk content API) | AOSP eccdata (Android's emergency-number database): IN 112 types ['AMBULANCE', 'FIRE', 'POLICE']. Sources agree it reaches: ambulance, fire, police. UK FCDO page checked: https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/india/getting-help (fetched 2026-10-29); page text: UK FCDO travel advice, Getting help: "Emergency services in India Telephone: 112 (ambulance, fire, police) These services provide support in English, Hindi and additional languages" (fetched 2026-10-29 via gov.uk content API). Cross-check (not a source): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_emergency_telephone_numbers — wikipedia agrees; 112.gov.in timed out from this environment so not fetched. 'languages' = the locale this entry is staged for (hi), not a verified statement of operator languages.
